newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds set sights on 102.60 for upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds set sights on 102.60 for upside.

text.p: September Bund options on LIFFE may be able to re-test 102.60 resistance on Friday as upside momentum gradually increases, technical analysts said.
Nico Bakker, analyst at ABM-AMRO Hoare Govett in Amsterdam said Bunds were a low trending market with the longer term framework defined by 101.50 on the downside and 103.50.

"With the break of 102.15 the upside bias is growing, but there is limited potential for now," Bakker said. Above 102.60, positive momentum would increase with the market heading towards 103.50 which is around the peaks set at the end of July.
By 0640 GMT, September Bunds were 0.05 up at 102.38.
Bakker pegged support initially at 102.30 which is around the previous top of the current consolidation phase.
"Aggressive traders should put their stops at 102.30, or may be 102.25. The real stop is at 102.15," Bakker said.
But while 102.30 held, the market was likely to extend gains to 102.60, which is the bottom of the previous trading range, and possibly to 103.50.
Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst, said Bunds were looking overstretched on the upside, and having trouble in breaking immediate resistance at around 102.40, 102.50.
Upside progress for Friday was limited, she added.
"They will continue to challenge the 102.40, 102.50 area but I doubt it will be a clear upside break," Gifford said.
The main support was 101.70, which is near the low on Wednesday, but Gifford said, "I doubt it will come back that far, not today anyway."
Traders said Friday's session was likely to be quiet with France and Italy closed for the Assumption Day holiday.
At the short end of the German curve, December Euromark futures stood 0.01 down on the day at 96.43.
